1.name: slices-emoji-html
1.title: Three regressions: Text slicing, splitting wide characters, HTML export classes
1.intro: Three bugs have been reported since the last release. Fix all three.
symptoms: Indexing a Text loses the style of the character: for Text("foo") with a red span over its first character, text[0] returns a plain "f" with no spans; it should be Text("f", spans=[Span(0, 1, "red")]).

rich.cells.split_text() goes wrong when the split falls inside a double-width character: split_text("\U0001f4a9\U0001f4a9xxxxxxxxxx", 3) returns ("\U0001f4a9", "\U0001f4a9xxxxxxxxxx"); it should split the second emoji and pad both sides with a space, giving ("\U0001f4a9 ", " xxxxxxxxxx").
Console.export_html() numbers its style classes from r0; they used to start at r1 (the first style is ".r1 {font-weight: bold}" in our saved exports), and the exported HTML no longer matches.
criteria: indexing a Text keeps the styles of the character
split_text splits inside a double-width character as described
export_html numbers its style classes from r1

2.name: highlight-tilde-ranges
2.title: Three regressions: empty highlight spans, the tilde's width check, Syntax ranges on the wrong line
2.intro: Three bugs have been reported since the last release. Fix all three.
symptoms: Highlighters add empty spans for named groups that match nothing: ReprHighlighter on "<foo>" gives Span(4, 4, "repr.tag_contents") before the tag end, and complex numbers such as "(3+2j)" get similar empty spans. A group that matches an empty string should add no span.

The check that a string is made only of single-cell characters (the fast path for measuring plain text) answers False for "~", the last printable ASCII character; the last character of each single-width range is left out.
Syntax.stylize_range() styles the line after the one asked for: a range starting at line 1 is drawn on line 2 (line numbers are 1-based). Tracebacks, which mark code this way, are affected too.
criteria: a highlighter adds no span for a group that matches nothing
"~" and the last character of each single-width range count as single-cell
stylize_range styles the lines it is given

3.name: column-nul-kilobyte
3.title: Three regressions: cursor column, zero-width characters, file sizes at the unit boundary
3.intro: Three bugs have been reported since the last release. Fix all three.
symptoms: Control.move_to_column(10, 20) produces "\x1b[10G\x1b[20B"; columns are 0-based in Rich and 1-based in the escape code, so it should be "\x1b[11G\x1b[20B".

Characters that should take no space are measured as one cell: cell_len(chr(0)) is 1 where every non-printable character below 32 should be 0, and console.rule("\u6b22\u8fce\uff01") on a 16-column console is no longer "\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500 \u6b22\u8fce\uff01 \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500".

The download column of a progress bar keeps sizes exactly at a unit boundary in the smaller unit: 500 of 1,000 bytes shows "500/1,000 bytes" where it should show "0.5/1.0 kB", and the binary units have the same problem at 1,024.
criteria: non-printable characters measure as zero cells and wide characters measure correctly
the download column uses the larger unit at a unit boundary

4.name: row-linerange-recursion
4.title: Three regressions: cursor row, the first line of a Syntax line range, a crash printing locals
4.intro: Three bugs have been reported since the last release. Fix all three.
symptoms: Control.move_to(x, y) puts the cursor one row too high: it produces "\x1b[10;6H" for (5, 10) where it should produce "\x1b[11;6H", so screen updates are drawn on the wrong rows.

A Syntax with a line_range shows the first line of the range without highlighting: with line_range=(2, 10) line 2 is plain text while lines 3 to 10 are coloured. It should be highlighted like the rest.

Printing a traceback with show_locals=True can crash inside Rich with "ZeroDivisionError: integer modulo by zero", raised while the Columns layout arranges the locals. We hit it printing an exception raised as its own cause (raise e from e) inside a pytest test.
criteria: move_to puts the cursor on the right row
the first line of a line range is highlighted

5.name: pad-justify-export
5.title: Three regressions: lines of exact length, full justification, empty export elements
5.intro: Three bugs have been reported since the last release. Fix all three.
symptoms: Segment.adjust_line_length() changes a line that already has the requested length: it should return the line as it is, but it appends an empty Segment(""), so a Panel's render_lines() output has an extra empty segment on lines that fit exactly.
Wrapping Text with justify="full" crashes with "IndexError: list index out of range" when a line needs extra spaces (the demo card, python -m rich, crashes this way).

Console.export_html() and Console.export_svg() produce extra empty elements where two styles meet: printing "[bold red]a[/][green]b[/] c" and exporting HTML gives ab, with an empty span and an extra style class that should not be there.
criteria: adjust_line_length leaves a line of the requested length unchanged
export_html and export_svg match the saved exports again

6.name: grid-edge-split-ranges
6.title: Three regressions: grid padding at the edge, splitting at the end of text, Syntax range columns
6.intro: Three bugs have been reported since the last release. Fix all three.
symptoms: A table with pad_edge=False keeps the padding on the right of its last column: Table.grid(padding=(0, 1)) with three columns of "aaa" exports "aaa aaa aaa " where it should be "aaa aaa aaa", and Columns layouts change width because of it.

rich.cells.split_text() crashes with "IndexError: list index out of range" when asked to split exactly at the end of text that ends in a grapheme cluster: split_text("\U0001f469\u200d\U0001f527", 2) should return ("\U0001f469\u200d\U0001f527", "").
Syntax.stylize_range() ignores the column it is given: every range starts one character before the start of its line instead of at the requested column.
criteria: pad_edge=False removes the padding on the right of the last column
split_text at the end of the text returns the whole text and an empty string
stylize_range starts at the requested column
